newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Viag hopeful of higher earnings in '97.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Viag hopeful of higher earnings in '97.

text.p: Earnings in the current year at German diversified utility giant Viag AG will at least match, or possibly exceed, those seen in 1996, the group's chairman told a news conference on Friday.

Last year saw a decline in group net profit at Viag to 1.06 billion marks ($622.8 million) from 1.32 billion marks a year earlier, but 1995 figures were inflated by lower tax charges, and developments in the first quarter gave rise to optimism, management board chairman Georg Obermeier said.
"The chances are good that we can lift sales in the current year and also maintain profits (before and after tax) at their current high level, or raise them slightly," Obermeier said.

In the first three months of the year, pre-tax profits grew to 674 million marks from 668 million marks, while group sales rose to 12.3 billion marks from 10.9 billion marks in the same quarter last year -- falling somewhat short of analysts' expectations.
"The fall in earnings in 1996 can be attributed to clearly higher tax on earnings. Our tax charges were unusually low in 1995 because we could offset taxes against previous losses," the group said.
In midday trade, Viag shares were quoted at 768.50 marks, down 2.50 marks.
The group is aiming for a return on capital employed of 10 percent in three to five years, up from six percent now, Obermeier said in an interview with Reuters Financial Televison.
Obermeier also said he was hopeful about a higher dividend.
"I am very optimistic of paying an increased dividend for 1997, but that is not a decision for this year."

For the current year, Obermeier said Viag plans 5.5 billion marks in investments, compared to around 5.3 billion marks last year. He said these would be divided half and half between tangible and financial investments.
Viag is currently trying to acquire a stake in the Berlin state utility Bewag along with its partners, fellow German utility PreussenElektra and Southern Company from the United States.

The acquistion is currently being examined by cartel authorities, as is its attempt to purchase a majority stake in the utility Isar Amper. Obermeier said he expected a decision from the cartel authorities in Berlin and Brussels during the summer.
Viag last month raised its stake in chemical group Th Goldschmidt AG to a majority stake, and it said some of the group's operations were an ideal complement to Viag's chemical division.
Overall, the main contributors to growth in the first quarter were Viag's speciality chemical unit SKW Trostberg and its utility Bayernwerk, the group said.

It also said that on an adjusted basis, to account for the extraordinary earnings from the sale of the Didier unit included in last year's numbers, the group's profits would have climbed by seven percent.
Earnings per share (EPS), calculated using the DVFA German analysts' method, was 37.10 marks per share. This was close to market expectations.
According to the DVFA figures, contributions from its energy division, led by Bayernwerk, accounted for 77 percent of Viag's earnings.
Viag said seven percent of its DVFA earnings came from chemicals, 16 percent from packaging and four percent from logistics.
